statement_record.book: For monoidal preorders P, Q, a monoidal monotone P → Q is a monotone map f with (a) I_Q ≤_Q f(I_P) and (b) f(p1) ⊗_Q f(p2) ≤_Q f(p1 ⊗_P p2); it is STRONG when both are equivalences (≤ both ways) and STRICT when both are equalities. The inequality direction makes this the lax notion.

Blind pass initially agreed with PRESENT (LaxMonoidalFunctor / MonoidalFunctor / StrictMonoidalFunctor give the book's lax/strong/strict trichotomy in the right orientation, and the cited lines are all exact: Functor/Structure/Monoidal.v:77 `Class MonoidalFunctor`, :110 `Class LaxMonoidalFunctor`, :138 `MonoidalFunctor_Is_Lax`, Functor/Structure/Monoidal/Strict.v:54 `Class StrictMonoidalFunctor`, Construction/Enriched/Two.v:175 `Record MonotoneMap` with Theorem EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone at :183). The overturn rests on ONE FALSE SENTENCE in the Phase-C strength_comparison: 'The extra fields the classes carry beyond the book's data (pure_left, pure_right, ap_assoc and the three coherence equations) are automatic in a thin category -- derivable from monotonicity plus (a)/(b) -- so nothing stronger is being demanded of a monoidal monotone.' The three coherence EQUATIONS are indeed automatic in a thin category. The three ISO fields are not. Read Functor/Structure/Monoidal.v:119-123: `pure_left {x} : I (x) F x ~= F (I (x) x)`, `pure_right {x} : F x (x) I ~= F (x (x) I)`, `ap_assoc {x y z} : (F x (x) F y) (x) F z ~= F (x (x) (y (x) z))` -- no `:=` default, hence REQUIRED data, and none of them is mentioned by lax_monoidal_unit_left / lax_monoidal_unit_right / lax_monoidal_assoc (:125-135). In the thin case an isomorphism is mutual <=, i.e. EQUALITY of elements. Under Definition 2.2 unitality and associativity are equations between ELEMENTS, so pure_left/pure_right collapse to f(p) ~= f(p) and are indeed free -- but ap_assoc becomes 'f(p1) (x) f(p2) (x) f(p3) ~= f(p1 (x) p2 (x) p3)', whose <= direction is condition (b) twice and whose >= direction is a GENUINE EXTRA REQUIREMENT. It fails for the book's own canonical lax-not-strong example, floor : (R, <=, 0, +) -> (N, <=, 0, +) of Example 2.42(ii): (floor 0.5 + floor 0.5) + floor 0 = 0 while floor(0.5 + (0.5 + 0)) = 1, and 1 <= 0 is false in (N, <=). Worse, taking p3 = I_P with a unit-preserving f the iso forces f(p1 (x) p2) ~= f(p1) (x) f(p2), i.e. in-tree 'lax' COLLAPSES TO STRONG in the thin case. So the book's primary notion -- the LAX monoidal monotone, the whole point of Definition 2.41's inequality direction -- has no faithful in-tree class; only the strong level (MonoidalFunctor) and the strict level (StrictMonoidalFunctor) match. Corroboration that the fields are real obligations and not bookkeeping: Functor/Structure/Monoidal/Id.v:83-85 discharges them for the IDENTITY functor with `apply tensor_assoc`, and Instance/Coq/Applicative.v:173-181 leaves the applicative-to-lax-monoidal instance COMMENTED OUT, so the only inhabitants of LaxMonoidalFunctor in-tree are Id, Compose, and hypotheses (Construction/DecoratedCospan.v:114 takes LM as a Context parameter). Also carried into problems[] as a library defect, since the class header at :44-47 asserts precisely the opposite. Fields corrected: classification, gap, statement_record.strength_comparison, and one added evidence entry (Id.v:83-85).

statement_record.book: Monoidal monotones are the preorder-level instance of monoidal functors (forward reference to the rough definition of symmetric monoidal functor, 6.68). What Definition 2.41 calls a monoidal monotone is more precisely a LAX monoidal monotone; the dual, OPLAX, notion reverses both inequalities: f(I_P) ≤_Q I_Q and f(p1 ⊗_P p2) ≤_Q f(p1) ⊗_Q f(p2). Oplaxity is not used in the book.
statement_record.intree: Class LaxMonoidalFunctor := { lax_pure : I ~> F I; ... lax_ap {x y} : F x ⨂ F y ~> F (x ⨂ y); ... } together with MonoidalFunctor_Is_Lax : MonoidalFunctor → LaxMonoidalFunctor.
